the perforant path projection into the hippocampus is a heterogeneous projection, and each of the hippocampal subregions has a unique role for the processing of environmental information.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the perforant path projection to the medial dorsal hippocampus is critical for spatial learning and memory, whereas the perforant path projections to the lateral and medial dorsal hippocampus are critical for nonspatial (object recognition) learning and memory.

the hippocampus is a highly plastic and complex structure that can process multiple types of information.
